drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you for your prompt response. 

We confirm that the intention behind the 'Disclosure Limits' section is not to introduce material new restrictions beyond those contained in the existing confidentiality obligations. Instead, it is meant to provide further clarity regarding the scope and types of permissible disclosures, and to address a potential aggregate information threshold for non-public data, as is sometimes customary in transactions of this nature. We are open to discussing the threshold figures and any carve-outs you may propose.

Regarding the discrepancy between the protection period and the overall term, our client's preference is to ensure that confidentiality protection subsists for a commercially reasonable period following the expiry of the agreement itself. The three-year period is intended to safeguard the most sensitive aspects of the disclosed information, as certain strategic or proprietary materials may retain commercial sensitivity well after the completion or cessation of discussions.

We look forward to your further comments, and have updated the draft accordingly.

edits.text: 6. DISCLOSURE LIMITS. The parties agree that disclosure of confidential information under this Agreement shall not, in aggregate, exceed the thresholds to be mutually agreed in writing. The intention is to provide clarity regarding the permissible categories and amounts of non-public information disclosed, without creating undue restrictions beyond existing confidentiality obligations. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this section shall limit the parties’ rights to disclose as otherwise permitted under this Agreement or by law.
